items.title: Ubuntu, African Ethics, and Human-Centred Artificial Intelligence in Project Management: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is progressively revolutionising project management by enhancing forecasting, planning, decision-making, risk evaluation, and organisational efficacy. Nevertheless, escalating apprehensions about trust, accountability, equity, transparency, and human supervision have underscored the necessity for governance strategies that transcend mere technical efficacy. This research performs a concept-focused systematic literature review to investigate the convergence of Ubuntu, African ethics, Human-Centred Artificial Intelligence (HCAI), and project governance. This research consolidates disparate knowledge domains related to responsible AI, HCAI, ethical leadership, stakeholder governance, organisational preparedness, and Ubuntu-informed leadership, stakeholder inclusivity, and a comprehensive Ubuntu-informed human-AI governance framework, utilising peer-reviewed literature from 2022 to 2026. This research posits that Ubuntu offers a unique governance viewpoint rooted in collective responsibility, relational leadership, and human dignity. The results indicate that Ubuntu-informed AI governance can assist African governments and policymakers in establishing ethical and responsible frameworks. This research establishes a basis for subsequent investigations on Ubuntu, artificial intelligence governance, and project management. The results underscore the significance of ethical leadership, stakeholder engagement, human supervision, and responsibility for project management professionals in responsible AI-driven project settings.

items.title: Understanding ChatGPT adoption among medical students: an integrated theoretical model of psychological barriers and individual factors
items.abstract: Background The growing adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly ChatGPT, has created new opportunities for medical education by supporting learning, problem-solving, and knowledge acquisition. However, evidence regarding the psychological and individual factors influencing ChatGPT adoption among medical students remains limited. This study develops and tests an integrated theoretical model that combines Privacy Theory, Technostress Theory, Affect Theory, Diffusion of Innovation Theory, and the Theory of Planned Behavior to explain ChatGPT adoption. Material and methods A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate medical students at King Faisal University, Saudi Arabia using a structured, self-administered questionnaire. The proposed model examined the effects of privacy concern, technophobia, guilt feelings, and innovativeness on behavioral intention and ChatGPT usage behavior, with behavioral intention serving as the mediating variable. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results The findings showed that innovativeness had a significant positive relationship with behavioral intention ( β = 0.579, p < 0.001), while behavioral intention had a strong positive relationship with ChatGPT usage behavior ( β = 0.777, p < 0.001). In addition, behavioral intention significantly mediated the relationship between innovativeness and ChatGPT usage behavior ( β = 0.450, p < 0.001). In contrast, privacy concern, technophobia, and guilt feelings were not significantly related to behavioral intention, and their indirect relationships with ChatGPT usage behavior were also not significant. Conclusion Within the proposed model, personal innovativeness was the only antecedent significantly associated with behavioral intention, whereas the psychological barriers were not statistically significant. By integrating five complementary theoretical perspectives into a single framework, this study extends current understanding of generative AI adoption in medical education and highlights behavioral intention as the key mechanism linking individual characteristics to actual use. The findings provide theoretical insights and practical guidance for promoting the responsible and effective integration of ChatGPT into medical education through initiatives that foster innovativeness and AI literacy.

items.title: Understanding Social Bias in Multimodal Learning Systems: A Taxonomy and Framework
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of multimodal learning systems across high-stakes applications has intensified concerns about fairness and social bias, yet existing research remains scattered across modalities, tasks, protected attributes, mitigation strategies, and evaluation methodologies. This survey provides an overview of fairness and social bias in multimodal artificial intelligence. By reviewing 44 papers and 16 datasets, we synthesize the current landscape of fairness research in multimodal systems and identify emerging challenges and research opportunities. Our primary contribution is twofold. First, we introduce a multi-dimensional taxonomy that organizes the literature across nine operational dimensions, providing a unified perspective on multimodal fairness research. Second, we propose an end-to-end operational lifecycle framework that illustrates how biases emerge within shared latent spaces and identifies targeted pre-processing, training-time, and post-training intervention strategies. Overall, this survey discusses key performance-fairness trade-offs and provides a structured roadmap for evaluating and mitigating bias, ultimately supporting the development of more equitable multimodal AI systems.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been a silent presence in research for several years, and through various technologies, AI has become ever-present in qualitative studies. As AI continues to proliferate and its use expands both outside and within scholarship, the use of AI in research has evolved from a resource for qualitative scholars to a tool for study participants to use as they engage with our research studies. We had separate encounters with research participants using AI to author narratives in our dissertation studies. Through examples from our studies, this article explores the impact of AI use by study participants.

items.title: User Preferences for Enhanced Robot Adaptation in Assistive Tasks
items.abstract: The adaptation of robot behaviour to each user can be seen as an ergonomic feature. Adaptation plays a key role in increasing human–robot interaction efficiency and safety, and this is especially relevant in assistive scenarios, where users may be unable to adapt to the robot or help in task execution. Robot adaptation may happen at different levels of abstraction, from low-level trajectory parameters to higher-level task concepts. These higher-level abstractions relate to human factors such as personal preferences on how the robot should perform the task. This chapter introduces the concept of user preferences to adapt the robot’s behaviour and also help in the robot’s decision-making, with a special focus on assistive robotic tasks such as dressing or feeding a user with mobility impairments. It also presents the challenges associated with adaptation in this kind of scenario, as well as some existing methods that may be used to adapt robot behaviour to high-level abstract preferences. Such adaptation makes it easier for the user to interact with the robot in a more efficient and comfortable manner, thus improving its ergonomics.

items.abstract: User-Centred Ecological Interface Design (UCEID) is a human factors framework designed to be used in the early stages of interface design. This suite of methods was used to determine what features Mobility as a Service (MaaS) required to not only be a genuinely useful and effective journey planning tool but also accessible to all ages and genders to ensure travel equity. Methods used included benchmarking MaaS apps, holding focus groups looking at in-app iconography, and Design with Intent workshops leading to design concepts and storyboards. As a result, design recommendations were provided to optimise the initial product design.

items.title: Validation of a computer-vision milking parlour monitoring system
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can help identify suboptimal milking practices and provide reports without time-consuming visits. The objective of this study was to validate a computer-vision milking parlour monitoring system (CVS, Cattle Care Inc.) by comparing its reports against trained human observers (n = 2, comparison method). A camera was installed in the parlour of two dairy farms in Ontario, Canada, one operating a herringbone parlour and the other a parallel parlour. Four one-hour segments (2 per farm), selected by the CVS, were independently analysed by human observers and the CVS. Prep-lag time, average unit-on time, turn time, and milking protocol deviations were assessed in each shift and compared between methods. For continuous variables, Lin’s concordance correlation coefficients (CCC) were calculated to evaluate the agreement between CVS and human observers; Bland–Altman plots were used to assess systematic bias. For categorical variables, the F-score was calculated to assess event-detection performance. The CCC for unit-on time (n=44 milking turns) was 0.999 (95% CI: 0.999-0.999), for prep-lag time (n = 214 cows) was 0.995 (95% CI: 0.994–0.996) and for turn time (n = 25 turns) was 0.998 (95% CI: 0.997–0.999). All protocol deviations flagged by the human observers (n = 51 events) were detected by the CVS; six towel misuse events detected by the CVS were missed by the human observers. An F-score of 1 was obtained for the CVS method. Under the conditions tested, the CVS demonstrated high agreement with human observations for prep-lag time, unit-on time, turn time, and milking-protocol deviations, while also identifying some events not detected by human observers. The assessed technology may complement human expertise by enabling more efficient and streamlined assessment of milking parlour performance.

items.title: Vibe Coding: An experiment with test-driven development
items.abstract: Abstract Context Conversational Large Language Models (CLLMs) can automatically generate code by collaborating with users through natural language. However, poor collaboration can lead to poor quality output. Objective This exploratory study aims to investigate how humans and CLLMs can collaborate as peers through vibe coding, an approach that integrates principles from prompt engineering, agile design, and human-AI co-creation to enhance collaboration. Method We designed four interaction models representing different collaboration patterns in the software development process: the solo model (human-only development), the collaborative model (human–CLLM collaboration), the fully automated model (development autonomously performed by a CLLM), and the agentic model (development autonomously performed by the MetaGPT X platform). Based on these models, we implemented corresponding Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflows using structured prompts and Python scripts. We then conducted a controlled pre-experimental study with TDD professionals to compare the solo and collaborative workflows. In addition, we performed repeated exploratory executions of fully automated and agentic workflows on the same development tasks to obtain complementary evidence. Results Our findings suggest that the choice of interaction model should depend on the development objective. Agentic workflows are best suited for rapid development and functionally correct production code but may introduce additional implementation complexity. However, they may also introduce additional implementation decisions that are not explicitly required by the functional specifications, resulting in untested decision points. In contrast, collaborative workflows produce higher-quality, better-organized test suites. Conclusions Our work explored how humans can collaborate with CLLMs in generating code in highly intensive and demanding development process. Our results also show that accurately reproducing development process workflows is yet an open problem, also in the new agentic technologies.

items.title: Virtualism: A Reserve-Based Income and Monetary Framework for the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is weakening the link between production and labor income on which capitalist economies distribute purchasing power. This paper argues that redistribution financed by taxation or public debt, including conventional universal basic income (UBI), cannot close this gap at scale, and proposes an alternative framework, Virtualism. Each person is endowed with a basic reserve equal to their remaining years up to an agreed lifespan (80 years), measured in hours (Time-Money), valued against a decent-living standard and released monthly to the family account on the condition of basic work: community service in one's own village. The reserve is allocated across four accounts (household 70%, enterprise 20%, village fund 5%, basic tax 5%), is non-inheritable and extinguished at death, while gains from its management are inheritable. Money is issued against this human reserve rather than through interest-bearing debt; existing wealth and prices are preserved through a one-time fixed conversion, after which exchange rates float. A collective per-capita production cap and a virtue rating that prices ethical conduct complete the framework. Illustrative calculations for Indonesia suggest that a debt-financed UBI at a decent-living standard would exceed ten times state revenue, whereas the proposed system requires no budgetary outlay and yields basic tax revenue of about IDR 1,680 trillion a year. The binding constraint shifts from finance to real production. The same formula applies in any currency: a United States illustration yields identical hours of life at a different money value, and a working web prototype demonstrates the mechanism. The paper discusses trade-offs, open questions, and a proposed one-year pilot in five villages on Adonara, Flores (1,250 people, about USD 8 million).

items.title: Vocal Loudness and Stability as Behavioral Indicators of Surgeons’ Non-Technical Skills
items.abstract: Non-technical skills (NTS) are essential for safe surgical teamwork, while objective measures of how surgeons communicate remain limited. This pilot study examined whether sentence-level vocal loudness and stability distinguish simulated good- and bad-NTS conditions and identified the voice features most sensitive to NTS differences. Three surgical education fellows completed three scenarios under both conditions. Good- and bad-NTS events were designed to reflect NOTSS scores of 4 and 1. Surgeon speech was isolated, vocal intensity was quantified using root-mean-square (RMS) amplitude, and sentences were classified as low, normal, or high volume relative to event-specific reference levels. Vocal stability was assessed using state entropy and state-persistence probability. Bad-NTS events showed greater loudness, more frequent extreme-volume states, higher entropy, and lower persistence, with moderate-to-large effects (|δ| ≥ .60). Mean event-level RMS, high-volume-state frequency, state entropy, and state persistence were the most sensitive features (|δ| > .80), supporting their use in objective NTS assessment.

Der Beitrag analysiert Potenziale und Grenzen KI-gestützter Anwendungen zur Erschließung von Normeninhalten für das berufliche Arbeiten und Lernen. Zugleich wird gezeigt, dass KI-generierte Antworten kritisch auf fachliche Richtigkeit und Normenkonformität geprüft werden müssen. Daraus ergeben sich neue Anforderungen für die berufliche Bildung im Bauwesen. Technical standards constitute a fundamental basis for professional practice in the construction industry. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems are transforming access to these standards and the development of normative professional knowledge. This paper examines the potential and limitations of AI-supported applications for facilitating access to the content of technical standards in vocational work and learning. It also demonstrates that AI-generated responses must be critically evaluated with regard to their technical accuracy and compliance with applicable standards. These developments give rise to new requirements for vocational education and training in the construction sector.

items.abstract: 💎 Solving the Global Data Crisis: Introducing VTAS-Hybrid Inventor: Tommi AronenPublication Date: October 9, 2026 Research Status: Experimental Benchmark Candidate 🌍 Why This Invention Changes the World Our modern society completely relies on data. Our digital photos, global banking transactions, medical research, and artificial intelligence models are all preserved inside massive data centers on physical magnetic tapes and optical media. However, due to the fundamental laws of physics, these physical materials inevitably degrade, fade, and accumulate microscopic scratches over decades. When a playback drive attempts to read this worn surface, severe data corruption occurs, leading to permanent information loss. While global technology conglomerates attempt to solve this lifespan crisis by developing expensive, exotic new materials in laboratories, the VTAS-Hybrid architecture developed by Tommi von Aronen introduces a complete revolution: it accepts material imperfection and rescues the data using software intelligence. 🧠 How VTAS-Hybrid Works (In Plain English) VTAS-Hybrid acts as an "intelligent brain" installed directly into the readout drive. Instead of blindly assuming the storage tape remains factory-fresh, it continuously measures and adapts to the material's real-time physical condition in milliseconds: Continuous Health Auditing: The drive scans microscopic pilot symbols embedded within the data stream, using them to map the exact degradation level of the material. Instant Flaw Adaptation: If the media encounters a physical scratch or debris, VTAS-Hybrid identifies the anomaly statistically and shifts its decision boundaries on the fly with lightning speed. The Uncertainty Map (Erasure Masking): If a specific bit is so faded that the drive is uncertain, it bypasses guessing and flags it with a "safety marker." This creates a precise map for the hardware Error Correction Coding (ECC), showing exactly which bits need to be mathematically repaired. 💰 Commercial and Industrial Value Massive Cost Reductions for Data Centers: Enterprises do not need to replace their existing infrastructure or buy expensive experimental materials. Budget-friendly storage media lasts decades longer because the drive's software algorithmically compensates for physical wear. Ironclad Software Robustness: The algorithm integrates strict industrial-grade safeguards that catch and isolate measurement errors, mathematical anomalies (like NaNs), and truncated blocks before they can cause silent data corruption. items.title: Warehouse logistics and task switching theory revisited: asymmetric height switching costs in order picking systems
items.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the impact of pick location height switching on task performance time in manual order picking systems. Drawing on task switching theory, we examine whether switching between ground- and chest-level pick locations increases task performance time, whether switching costs are asymmetric, and whether item weight strengthens possible differences between ground-to-chest and chest-to-ground switches. Design/methodology/approach We adopt a two-stage approach that combines internal validity and operational generalizability. First, a controlled eye-tracking experiment simulates a simplified order picking scenario to explore the cognitive mechanisms underlying visual search when repeating versus switching pick location heights. Second, we analyze 3,537,973 pick location visits from a German grocery retail warehouse to test the effects of pick location height switching in a real-world operational environment with professional order pickers. Findings The eye-tracking experiment provides mechanism-oriented evidence that switching between pick location heights increases visual search time and reorientation demands under controlled conditions. The archival field study complements these behavioral insights by showing that height switching is associated with longer task performance time. It further shows that switching costs depend on direction, with ground-to-chest switches being more time-consuming than chest-to ground switches. This directional difference becomes more pronounced as item weight increases. Practical implications The findings suggest that warehouse managers should consider not only the frequency but also the direction of height switches when designing picking sequences. Batching and routing algorithms could incorporate switching costs as a weighted parameter, with particular attention to ground-to-chest switches involving heavier items. However, reducing height switches should be balanced against ergonomic risks, as long sequences of ground-level picks may increase repetitive bending and musculoskeletal strain. Originality/value This study provides the first empirical evidence on pick location height switching in warehouse operations and extends task switching theory to a new operational context. By combining mechanism-oriented eye-tracking evidence with large-scale field data, we show that height switching is associated with asymmetric switching costs and provide insights into the cognitive and motor reorientation processes that may underlie these effects.

items.title: What “Digitization” Means for the Limbe Deep Sea Port (Cameroon) Project: Definitions, Components, Pathways, and Implications
items.abstract: Digitization in the deep sea port context is often invoked as shorthand for technological modernization, yet its operational meaning and implications vary widely by place. This paper explicates what “digitization” means for the Limbe Deep Sea Port in Cameroon by situating the concept within port operational processes, stakeholder relationships, governance environments, and socioeconomic constraints specific to Limbe and comparable West/Central African ports. Drawing on an interdisciplinary desk-based literature review of academic studies, international agency reports, industry white papers, and regional policy documents, the study adopts a conceptual-analytical approach to define digitization as the systematic conversion and integration of analogue and paper-based port procedures into interoperable digital systems that enable real-time data exchange, automated workflows, evidence-based decision-making, and secure electronic transactions across the port ecosystem. The paper disaggregates digitization into technological (TOS, PCS, VTMS, IoT, analytics, blockchain, cybersecurity), organizational (process re-engineering, governance, procurement), human factors (skills, roles, change management), and regulatory (single window, data governance) dimensions. It identifies measurable indicators to assess progress—transaction digitalization rate, vessel turnaround time, dwell time, customs clearance time, system uptime, and workforce certification rates—and outlines likely benefits (efficiency, transparency, environmental monitoring, regional connectivity) and risks (digital divides, cyber threats, governance bottlenecks, finance constraints). The analysis highlights contextual enablers and barriers for Limbe, including infrastructure, institutional capacity, financing options, and regional integration imperatives. The paper concludes with policy and operational recommendations that prioritize staged interventions—low‑complexity quick wins, mid‑term integration, and long‑term smart-port capabilities—anchored in inclusive governance, blended finance, workforce development, and cyber resilience. The findings aim to provide a clear, practical, and academically grounded definition of digitization tailored to Limbe’s developmental and geopolitical realities. items.title: What If AI Agents Had to Prove What Actually Happened Before Being Allowed to Continue?
items.abstract: An AI agent may be authorized to act—but what happens when the real-world result differs from what was authorized? Should that agent still be allowed to continue? As frontier AI models evolve into autonomous systems capable of executing payments, transmitting sensitive information, modifying infrastructure, invoking privileged tools, and controlling physical devices, a fundamental security question emerges: Why should authorization granted before an action remain sufficient when its actual consequences have not yet been independently verified? This paper proposes a different model of machine authority: “Computation is not authority to act. Authority must be earned from the real execution path, not granted indefinitely per session.” The research introduces Receipt-Gated Interim Effectuation Validation (IEV), an execution-control architecture in which a consequential operation may first produce a real but strictly bounded effect. Protected evidence of what actually occurred is subsequently examined by an independent validator. Only successful validation establishes the protected continuation condition required for a subsequent, potentially broader effect. The distinction is fundamental: the AI agent's assertion that an action succeeded is not proof that it happened correctly, and a receipt alone is not authorization to continue. The proposed architecture incorporates: Real-effect validation: Verification of actual outcomes rather than reliance solely on predicted behavior, proposed commands, or self-reported success. Receipt-gated continuation: Subsequent effectuation depends on protected validation of the preceding bounded effect. Independent execution authority: Separation of the AI computation environment from protected policy, credential, validation, and effectuation components. Software–hardware enforcement: Continuation conditions realized through cryptographic objects, derived or split keys, protected state, hardware latches, or equivalent mechanisms. Finality Sink verification: Independent checks at the effect-capable boundary, including act, destination, scope, phase, freshness, and revocation conditions. Taint and provenance controls: Consideration of untrusted inputs, prompt-injection exposure, credential surrogation, and privilege-separated execution. Fail-closed recovery: Explicit handling of missing receipts, uncertain outcomes, conflicting authentic evidence, validator compromise, crash recovery, and unauthorized retries. Controlled escalation: Protected human review, bounded automated remediation, reduced-scope continuation, and termination where required. The paper develops a formal protocol vocabulary, validation predicates, continuation mechanisms, six conformance profiles, implementation-invariance rules, illustrative workflows, and an analytical model of residual exposure. Potential applications include frontier AI agent infrastructure, autonomous tool execution, cloud and network operations, financial transactions, critical infrastructure, and robotic systems. The central research proposition is that AI safety should not end at the moment permission is granted. For consequential autonomous operations, the authority to proceed can be made technically dependent on independently verified evidence of what actually occurred. This publication presents a proposed architecture and analytical design, not an experimentally validated production system. It does not establish that any existing commercial platform implements the proposed mechanisms. Patent disclosure: The architecture described in this publication is identified as patent pending under Indian Patent Office application 202631117633, titled “Systems and Methods for Cryptographically Staged Effectuation with Verified Partial Effect, Receipt-Bound Full Effectuation, and Software-Hardware Enforcement.” Patentability, enforceable scope, and relationships to other technologies are not determined by this publication. Independent technical review, adversarial evaluation, implementation criticism, and discussion of related prior art are welcomed.

items.title: What Is the Best Word to Describe AI Uncertainty: Confidence, Certainty, Reliability, or Accuracy?
items.abstract: AI systems are increasingly common in decision-making tasks. However, these systems often generate probabilistic responses, resulting in uncertainty in their outputs. Understanding this uncertainty can help users make robust decisions, such as when to trust the agent and whether to seek more information. Interpreting uncertainty is not always straightforward, though; past work shows there is variability in how people interpret probabilistic information (e.g., weather forecasts). This study builds on that research by analyzing how people interpret probabilistic AI responses. In this survey-based experiment ( N = 632), participants interpreted AI uncertainty statements. The word used to describe the uncertainty (confidence, certainty, reliability, or accuracy) varied between trials. Participants often treated confidence and certainty as indicators of how sure the agent was about its output, whereas interpretations of reliability and accuracy were more variable. These findings can guide how AI systems communicate uncertainty, supporting more accurate user interpretations and robust decision-making.

items.title: When One Size Doesn’t Fit All: Efficacy Assessment of an Engineering Control for Endoscopic Procedures
items.abstract: Studies report an elevated prevalence of endoscopy-related musculoskeletal disorders in gastroenterologists. Interventions primarily address work environment and work organization, not tool design (the endoscope). This study evaluated an add-on adjustable support strap designed to reduce the workload of the user’s left hand, which operates the endoscope’s control section. Study participants (four women, seven men) were experienced in endoscopy. Each participant performed two simulated colonoscopies with the support strap and two without (within-subjects design). Effects of the support strap were assessed using normalized muscle activity (nEMG) from surface electrodes over finger and wrist flexors and extensors and trapezius m., video, and usability data. With the strap, nEMG was reduced in most muscles for three participants (all women); mixed results for four, and no reduced nEMG for four others (all men). Mode of ratings of usability, usefulness, and desirability were 7, 5, 5, respectively (7 = very good). Results suggest benefits for some users.

items.title: Who Controls the Agents? AI Agent Orchestration as the New Security Perimeter
items.abstract: This presentation examines artificial intelligence agent orchestration as an emerging security perimeter in modern multi-agent systems. It explores how increasing agent autonomy, delegation mechanisms, tool integration, and inter-agent communication introduce new cybersecurity risks and governance challenges. The presentation analyzes major orchestration architectures, including deterministic workflows, orchestrator–worker systems, agent handoffs, decentralized multi-agent configurations, and learned orchestration. Particular attention is given to the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent2Agent (A2A) communication, trust boundaries, access control, and security vulnerabilities arising from interactions between autonomous agents and external tools. Drawing on recent cybersecurity incidents, technical standards, and research published in 2025–2026, the presentation evaluates the effectiveness and limitations of multi-agent architectures and discusses approaches to secure orchestration, verification, accountability, and human oversight. The central argument is that cybersecurity in agentic AI systems depends not only on individual model reliability but also on the governance and security of the entire orchestration process. Presented in connection with the V International Conference “Challenges and Reality of the IT-Space: Software Engineering and Cybersecurity” (SECS-2026), October 29–30, 2026, Kyiv, Ukraine (online).

items.title: ZERO TRUST FOR MCP-CONNECTED ENTERPRISE AI AGENTS
items.abstract: Enterprise AI agents now read tickets, documents, and web pages and then act on what they find through tool protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Because an agent combines untrusted input with delegated privileges, it creates a path from attacker-influenced content to privileged action that earlier Zero Trust programs did not anticipate. This article examines how the principles of NIST SP 800-207 should be extended for agents. It compares five approaches that organizations use to give agents access to enterprise systems, from shared API keys to task-scoped delegated tokens enforced at a gateway, and evaluates them against five attack classes: indirect prompt injection, tool poisoning, confused-deputy misuse, token theft and replay, and excessive agency. An exposure analysis of a representative service-desk agent shows that task-scoped, audience-bound, sender-constrained tokens reduce exposure by about five orders of magnitude compared with a shared key, while gateway mediation constrains what a hijacked agent can do with the access that remains. The article closes with an adoption roadmap and measures of progress.

items.title: О регламентации электронного документооборота - 19 принципов, которых нет в ITILWhat this article is about and what you will gain. This article is for those who manage critical information systems in large enterprises and the public sector. It presents 19 principles that cannot be circumvented, a three-lines-of-defense model, practical cases on protecting the security of your systems, their owners, operators, and users, and the role of the incident manager with veto power. The material is based on 26 years of experience and has been validated in a system with 10,000+ users and 3,000+ legal entities. Who it is for. IT directors, owners, operators, and technical support operators of critical information systems, EDI product owners, heads of technical support and maintenance services, methodologists, and system ideologists. Why this matters right now. Ten to fifteen years ago, electronic document interchange was seen as a convenient add-on to paper workflows: files, folders, approval routes. Today the situation has changed fundamentally — and in several directions at once: 1. Information systems have become incomparably more complex. A modern EDI system is not a "folder with files." It is dozens of integrations: with HR systems, with the Unified State Register of Legal Entities, with electronic signature systems, with external counterparties, with mobile applications, with reporting systems. Each integration is a point where a technical action can become a legal one. 2. Legislation has become more complex and stricter. Requirements for information protection are constantly growing. FSTEC orders, requirements for government information systems, personal data systems, and critical information infrastructure are not "recommendations" but mandatory norms. A regulation written five years ago may no longer comply with any current requirement — and no one will know until an inspection or an incident occurs. 3. Supervision over personal data violations has become stricter. Fines under Federal Law No. 152-FZ have risen to RUB 20 million. Each identified document containing personal data in an unintended system is qualified as a separate violation. 4. Electronic signatures have turned document flow into a legally significant process. Under Federal Law No. 63-FZ, an electronically signed document is equated to a paper document with a handwritten signature. This means that any administrative action with such a document — replacing a file, deleting metadata, adding a scan that differs from the signed version — is not a "correction" but potential falsification of evidence or official forgery (Articles 292, 303 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation). 5. Artificial intelligence without principles will turn chaos into chaos squared. AI does not account for legal risks unless it has been told to. If AI is implemented in a system without described processes, unified approaches, and principles, it does not eliminate chaos — it scales it. The only way to use AI safely is to describe the principles first, and automate afterwards. What this means for EDI regulation. All five factors converge at a single point: a regulation built solely on ITIL practices, GRC requirements, and HRO principles no longer protects. It describes processes but does not answer the question of what to do if a technical action is a legal act. It assumes that principles are already established — but does not say where they come from. It describes reliability — but does not provide a structure. That is why today we need principles that stand before methodologies and beyond their scope. Principles that cannot be circumvented by an order, by urgency, or by personal agreements. Principles that protect the system before it becomes a source of legal risk.

items.abstract: Аннотация. Статья посвящена проблематике, включающей оценку ожиданий медицинских работников в отношении влияния ИИ-агентов на организацию медицинской помощи и выявление межсекторных различий. В исследовании для сбора эмпирических данных использован метод анкетного опроса экспертов амбулаторно-стационарного звена государственных и частных медицинских организаций. В оценках использованы 10-балльные шкалы, агрегированные в домены эффективности, нагрузки, безопасности/доверия, экономики и ИТ-готовности. В результате исследования выявлено, что во всех доменах получены значения выше нейтрального уровня, а наивысшие — по безопасности пациентов. Выявлен высокий потенциал ИИ-агентов для оптимизации клинико-административных процессов. Проведенные расчеты продемонстрировали, что статистически значимых различий между секторами не имеется, но при этом сохраняется умеренный скепсис в отношении ИТ-готовности и передачи ИИ критически важных решений. Сделан вывод о том, что ИИ-агенты обладают значительным потенциалом трансформации системы здравоохранения, однако его реализация требует взвешенного подхода, сочетающего максимальное использование технологий с ответственным управлением присущими им рисками и неопределённостями. Annotation. The article is devoted to the problematics, including the assessment of expectations of medical workers regarding the impact of AI agents on the organization of medical care and the identification of intersectoral differences. In the study, the method of questionnaire survey of experts of the outpatient-inpatient link of public and private medical organizations was used to collect empirical data. In the assessments, 10-point scales were used, aggregated into domains of efficiency, load, safety/trust, economy and IT readiness. As a result of the study, it was revealed that in all domains, values above the neutral level were obtained, and the highest — on patient safety. The study identified a high potential for AI agents to optimize clinical and administrative processes. The calculations showed that there were no statistically significant differences between the sectors, but there was still moderate skepticism about the IT readiness and transfer of critical decisions to AI. The study concluded that AI agents have significant potential to transform the healthcare system, but their implementation requires a balanced approach that combines the maximum use of technology with responsible management of the inherent risks and uncertainties.

items.abstract: Выявлена роль объективной и согласованной оценки со стороны родителей и тренера, как фактора эффективного формирования внутренней мотивации достижений у младших школьников, занимающихся в спортивной секции карате Киокушинкай. В ходе исследования разработан и апробирован комплексный диагностический инструмент, включающий два парных опросника для родителей и тренеров, позволяющих оценить спортивную вовлечённость, психологическое благополучие и уровень поддержки ребёнка. Основные результаты показали высокий уровень мотивации у всех обследуемых, при этом статистический анализ (t-критерий Стьюдента и U-критерий Манна-Уитни) подтвердил отсутствие значимых расхождений между восприятием двух групп взрослых, что создаёт эффект «психологического резонанса». Установлено, что совпадение объективных оценок родителей и тренера обеспечивает когнитивную ясность и эмоциональную безопасность ребёнка, тогда как их расхождение порождает мотивационный вакуум и риск выученной беспомощности. Перспективы исследования включают масштабирование предложенного диагностического комплекса на другие виды спорта и возрастные группы, а также разработку программ психолого-педагогического сопровождения младших школьников при занятиях спортом. This article explores the role of objective and coordinated assessment by parents and coaches in developing intrinsic motivation for achievement in primary school students enrolled in a Kyokushinkai karate sports section.The study developed and tested a comprehensive diagnostic tool, including two paired questionnaires for parents and coaches, to assess the child's athletic involvement, psychological well-being, and level of support.The key findings revealed high levels of motivation across all subjects, while statistical analysis (Student's t-test and Mann-Whitney U-test) confirmed the absence of significant differences between the perceptions of the two groups of adults, creating a "psychological resonance" effect.It was found that convergence between objective assessments by parents and coaches ensures cognitive clarity and emotional security for the child, while discrepancies between them create a motivational vacuum and the risk of learned helplessness.Future research prospects include scaling the proposed diagnostic complex to other sports and age groups, as well as developing programs for psychological and pedagogical support for primary school students during sports activities.

items.title: Цифровая грамотность в вопросах здравоохранения среди медсестер амбулаторных клиник (обзор литературы)
items.abstract: Аннотация. Актуальность исследования определена тем, что уровень цифровой грамотности в вопросах здоровья среди медицинских сестер амбулаторно-поликлинических учреждений во всем мире варьируется он выше у тех, кто проходит целевое обучение. В исследовании проанализированы и систематизированы научные работы за 2021—2025 годы, посвященные определениям и компонентам цифровой грамотности в сфере здоровья, используемым цифровым инструментам, методам самооценки, отношению медсестер к цифровизации, а также национальным особенностям цифровой грамотности медицинских сестер. Доказано, что наиболее распространенными инструментами повышения уровня цифровизации амбулаторных клиник являются электронные медицинские карты, телемедицинские консультации, образовательные порталы для пациентов, системы удаленного мониторинга и решения на основе искусственного интеллекта. В результате проведения вторичного анализа данных выявлено, что медицинские сестры в целом положительно относятся к цифровым технологиям, но их внедрение ограничивается нехваткой времени, технических ресурсов и недостаточной интеграцией цифровых инструментов в рабочие процессы. Сделан вывод о том, что для повышения уровня цифровой зрелости и расширения перечня цифровых компетенций медицинских сестер требует целенаправленных специализированных инфраструктурных преобразований, включающих в себя организацию образовательных программ. Разработаны практические рекомендации, включающие стандартизацию оценки, интеграцию цифровых компетенций в учебные программы и применение контекстно-ориентированных подходов к обучению медицинских сестер амбулаторных клиник. Annotation. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that the level of digital literacy in health issues among nurses in outpatient clinics around the world varies, and it is higher among those who undergo targeted training. The study analyzes and systematizes scientific works from 2021 to 2025 on the definitions and components of digital literacy in the field of health, the digital tools used, self-assessment methods, nurses' attitudes towards digitalization, and the national characteristics of digital literacy among nurses. It has been proven that the most common tools for increasing the level of digitalization in outpatient clinics are electronic medical records, telemedicine consultations, educational portals for patients, remote monitoring systems, and artificial intelligence-based solutions. A secondary data analysis revealed that nurses generally have a positive attitude towards digital technologies, but their implementation is limited by a lack of time, technical resources, and insufficient integration of digital tools into work processes. It is concluded that in order to increase the level of digital maturity and expand the list of digital competencies of nurses, it requires targeted specialized infrastructure transformations, including the organization of educational programs. Practical recommendations have been developed, including the standardization of assessment, the integration of digital competencies into educational programs, and the application of context-based approaches to training nurses in outpatient clinics.

items.title: "Hot-Blooded" vs "Cold-Blooded": Simulating the Behavioral Phenotypes of Childhood Aggression via Generative Agents
items.abstract: This study examines the construct validity of LLM-based generative agents in simulating reactive, proactive, and co-occurring aggression in children. Four distinct agents were instantiated using a theory-driven parameterization grounded in the social information processing model. A total of 1,920 simulation runs were conducted across eight social scenarios, employing a hybrid blind-coding pipeline to extract 32 quantitative behavioral indicators. Results demonstrate robust discriminant validity relative to a non-aggressive baseline, with large effect sizes. High cross-seed reliability confirms that behavioral differentiation is driven by underlying psychological parameters rather than model stochasticity. Qualitative narrative analyses further converged with established empirical literature. Overall, these findings indicate that theory-parameterized LLM agents can accurately reproduce distinct aggression subtypes, offering a scalable, highly controllable framework for hypothesis generation, intervention piloting, and the refinement of psychological measurement tools.

items.title: "Smarter but Not Wiser": A Transdisciplinary CFA-GRM Simulation Pipeline for Mapping Human–GenAI Interaction
items.abstract: Background The integration of Generative AI (GenAI) in higher education creates a paradox between technical efficiency and cognitive depth. Current institutional responses rely more on fragmented oversight than on ecology- and process-oriented assessment. There is a lack of diagnostic tools to map psychometric thresholds when strategic cognitive shifts transition into functional dependence. Methods We present a simulation-based methodological framework using the Tripartite Confirmatory Factor Analysis–Graded Response Model (CFA-GRM). Grounded in the cognitive-affective-conative tripartite model, this study uses a Monte Carlo simulation (N = 1,000) to demonstrate how latent interaction pathways can be structurally validated and how item parameters can be calibrated against a pre-specified diagnostic threshold ( θ ≈ 0.5), with a replication study to establish parameter recovery. Results Across 200 replications at each of N = 1,000 and N = 300, all 400 converged with admissible solutions and recovered the generating parameters with maximum absolute relative bias of 0.040; interval coverage met conventional criteria for 11 of 15 parameter groups at N = 1,000 and 8 of 15 at N = 300. In the single illustrative dataset, the fit is near-perfect (robust CFI = 0.995, RMSEA = 0.010) because the generating and estimated models coincide, a property of the design rather than evidence for the model. Test information peaks at θ ≈ 0.07–0.22, not at the proposed threshold of θ ≈ 0.5. Furthermore, we introduce a Transdisciplinary Calibration Matrix that translates these psychometric signals into context-specific pedagogical interventions across four epistemic layers, in line with SDG 4. Conclusions This study does not claim empirical generalization. It provides a methodological blueprint, a recovered parameter set, and a shared diagnostic language for future empirical work on the ethical and adaptive integration of GenAI in higher education, aligned with SDG 4.

items.title: 14 AI Paradoxes
items.abstract: Fourteen AI Paradoxes: A Collection of Philosophical and Algorithmic Dilemmas By Tanuj Arora (2026) This publication presents a collection of fourteen conceptual paradoxes and philosophical thought experiments exploring the inherent tensions, unintended consequences, and ethical dilemmas associated with artificial intelligence. Each paradox examines a scenario in which the pursuit of technological perfection, algorithmic efficiency, or automated intelligence creates an unexpected conflict with human values, autonomy, identity, or societal well-being. The collection encompasses questions surrounding artificial intelligence, competitive optimization, autonomous decision-making, synthetic digital ecosystems, recursive learning, predictive control, cognitive dependency, digital identity, simulated empathy, privacy, and algorithmic governance. Through fourteen distinct scenarios, the work raises a central philosophical question: Can artificial intelligence achieve its intended objectives so effectively that it ultimately undermines the very purpose for which it was created? These paradoxes are presented as conceptual explorations rather than formally established logical contradictions. Their purpose is to encourage philosophical reflection, critical discussion, and interdisciplinary inquiry into the evolving relationship between humanity and intelligent machines. The collection is intended for researchers, philosophers, technologists, AI developers, and readers interested in the ethical and existential implications of artificial intelligence.

items.title: A 3D Characterization Framework for Intelligent Sequential Decision Making
items.abstract: Puzzles are widely used to evaluate the reasoning capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) systems for sequential decision making, yet approaches originating from different paradigms are rarely compared under unified conditions. To address this gap, we introduce a three-dimensional characterization framework that enables the analysts of AI methods by 1) projecting them to the Markov decision process (MDP) sequential decision making formalism, 2) degree of autonomy through human prior ranking of their designs and, 3) skill and computational cost. Using this framework, we analyze how representative graph-based, reinforcement learning, and large language model (LLM)-based approaches differ in their design choices and performance characteristics, instantiated respectively by Neurosolver, forward-backward reinforcement learning (FBRL), and automated thought-of-search (AutoToS), including a double-agent extension of thought-of-search (DA-ToS). The analysis relies on the Tower of Hanoi puzzle that provides a controlled benchmark with well-defined rules and scalable complexity, enabling consistent comparison across increasing problem sizes. The 3D characterization reveals that LLM-based methods, due to their weakly constrained action-space design, shift complexity from architecture to inference-time verification, leading to substantially higher memory and runtime costs than Neurosolver and FBRL.

items.title: A Blockchain and AI-Driven Framework for Decentralized Peer-to-Peer Skill Exchange Ecosystems
items.abstract: This chapter, per the authors, introduces the Decentralized Skill Exchange Network (DSEN), a unified sociotechnical framework reconstituting peer-mediated learning on Web3 foundations. Centralized learning platforms consolidate credential authority, behavioral data, and recommendation logic within single institutional entities, producing systems that are opaque, privacy-compromising, and resistant to learner agency. DSEN integrates four architecturally interdependent components: Ethereum-compatible smart contracts on Polygon Layer-2; a FedProx-based federated recommendation engine trained on locally held device data; W3C-compliant Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials for self-sovereign identity; and a token-governed incentive economy sustaining peer knowledge exchange without institutional intermediaries. Drawing on trustworthy federated reputation systems, Proof-of-Learning consensus, personalized federated recommender architectures, blockchain-enabled value co-creation theory, cross-chain interoperability, and FL-KG-LLM convergence research.

items.title: A conditional transfer for colourings of R^n, with the conditional consequence χ(R^3) ≥ 7
items.abstract: Assume Theorem 2.3 (rigidity of wild character laws) of the OpenAI preprint The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable. We prove that, for every n ≥ 2 and every set Λ of positive real algebraic numbers, a Λ-avoiding k-colouring of Rn (with no regularity assumption) yields a conull Borel partition of Rn into k sets, each containing no two points at a distance in Λ. Consequently, conditionally on that theorem, χ(Rn) ≥ ⌈1/m1(Rn)⌉, where m1(Rn) is the supremum of the upper densities of measurable sets avoiding distance 1. With the published bound on m1(R3) (DeCorte, de Oliveira Filho and Vallentin) this gives χ(R3) ≥ 7 (previously known lower bound: 6, Nechushtan 2002). We also derive conditional consequences for unbounded and m-element sets of forbidden distances and for finitary fractional chromatic parameters, whose conditional novelty lies in dimensions 2 and 3. For n ≥ 4 and distances with rational squares, James Davies (arXiv:2610.12301) has independently proved, unconditionally and by a different method, that the chromatic and measurable chromatic numbers coincide; his theorems do not cover dimensions 2 and 3. The transfer in the plane is due to OpenAI; our contribution is its extension to higher dimensions, which is new for n = 3. Status. All main results are conditional on Theorem 2.3 of OpenAI's preprint (github.com/openai/math, item 158), which has not been refereed. The note was written with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic), directed by the author, who is not a professional mathematician, and was checked by independent AI referee passes (OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini). It has not yet been reviewed by a human expert. Corrections are very welcome.

items.title: A deep generative adversarial framework with rat-optimized feature selection for efficient intrusion detection in large-scale cloud network traffic environments
items.abstract: Abstract Cloud computing is a fundamental paradigm in modern computing; however, its distributed and multi-tenant nature increases exposure to cyber threats, making effective intrusion detection essential. Despite recent advances in artificial intelligence–based intrusion detection systems (IDS), many existing approaches remain sensitive to class imbalance, computationally demanding, and insufficiently robust under large-scale network traffic conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an AI-driven intrusion detection framework, termed Secured Deep Generative Adversarial Rat-Optimized Diagonal Matrix (SDGA-RODM), designed for efficient intrusion detection in large-scale cloud network traffic environments. The proposed framework integrates three key components: (i) a mean divergence regularization (MDR)–based preprocessing strategy to mitigate class imbalance without altering intrinsic data distributions; (ii) a rat-optimized diagonal matrix score (RODMS)–based feature selection mechanism to derive compact and discriminative feature subsets; and (iii) a Wasserstein generative adversarial learning–based classifier (DWGALC) to enhance robustness under complex and imbalanced attack patterns. Extensive experiments conducted on the LUFlow and CIC-IDS-2017 benchmark datasets demonstrate that SDGA-RODM achieves improved performance compared with the evaluated representative IDS methods, including deep learning, ensemble-based, and optimization-driven approaches, achieving up to 6–8% improvement in detection accuracy, 15–40% reduction in classification error, and up to 30% reduction in training time under imbalanced traffic conditions. These results indicate that SDGA-RODM provides an effective and computationally efficient intrusion detection framework, demonstrating promising performance and robustness under controlled benchmark and simulation-based settings representative of cloud network traffic environments.

items.title: A feasibility study investigating quantitative and qualitative effects of exercise in the workplace during work time for menopausal women
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the feasibility of exercise classes undertaken in the workplace during work time in healthy menopausal women, and to study the potential benefits of this intervention. STUDY DESIGN: Of the 28 women (54.3 ± 6.5 years old; 162.6 ± 7.6 cm; 65.6 ± 12.5 kg) enrolled in the study, 22 completed it. It consisted in two testing sessions before and immediately after a 12-week exercise intervention that comprised two exercise classes (a choice from body conditioning, Zumba Gold, Pilates and high-intensity interval training) and two independent exercise sessions (exercise and timing of their choice) weekly. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Feasibility outcomes, including drop-out, retention and compliance, were measured during the intervention, and semi-structured interviews were conducted post-intervention. Psychological outcomes, menopause symptoms, physical activity levels and anthropometric and fitness variables were measured before and immediately after the intervention. RESULTS: Participants' drop-out, retention and compliance were 14.3%, 78.6% and 79%, respectively. The exercise programme had a positive effect in four main areas: positive organisational work culture, impact on menopausal physiological outcomes, impact on menopausal psychological outcomes, and improvements and growth for the programme. Finally, participation in the intervention was associated with favourable changes in body fat in the trunk, physical performance, menopause symptoms, mental health, and integrated and intrinsic motivation; however, the absence of a control group precludes causal inference. CONCLUSIONS: A workplace physical activity intervention during work time for menopausal women is feasible and was associated with favourable changes in several psychological and physical outcomes after 12 weeks, although the lack of a control group limits our ability to attribute these changes solely to the intervention.

items.title: A Machine Learning Framework for Startup Investor Matchmaking to Enhance Sustainable Innovation
items.abstract: Accelerating sustainable innovation is a critical mandate for emerging economies. However, the high failure rate of startups, primarily driven by inefficient founder-investor alignment and information asymmetry, remains a systemic obstacle. In Indonesia, this challenge is further exacerbated by traditional matchmaking processes that rely on social networks, often excluding high-potential Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). This study introduces and validates Artificial Intelligence Machine Learning Excellence Economy (AIMEE), a novel hybrid matchmaking framework designed to democratize access to capital and accelerate the twin transition of digitalization and sustainability. Utilizing a pilot dataset of 94 startup-investor pairs from five provinces in Java, we developed a policy-aware algorithm that integrates financial metrics with five entrepreneurial dimensions, including Sovereignty Scores based on alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The framework employs a lightweight neural network optimized with SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) to address data scarcity and class imbalance. Empirical validation shows that AIMEE achieves an F1-Score of 0.83, Recall of 0.82, and ROC-AUC of 0.89, significantly outperforming traditional Random Forest baselines by 12%. The model effectively identifies patterns of potential collaboration, overcoming the limitations of rigid networking. These findings confirm that AI-driven matchmaking can serve as a robust digital infrastructure to operationalize the Asta Cita vision and SDG 9, contributing to a more inclusive, resilient, and competitive innovation ecosystem in Indonesia.
